title: Bryteway Capital SOC2/ISO27001 posture readout & KMS/RBAC playbook
summary: High-level SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture readout. Covered Type II report availability, Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO integration options, audit log retention, data residency constraints, and KMS/encryption workflows. Agreed to share artifacts and schedule a technical deep-dive bench run for private deployment latency and KMS integration.
action_items: Ethan Park: Share SOC 2 Type II report PDF and Trust Center link (by 2026-09-01)
Sofia Martinez: Prepare short tech note on KMS key flow for private deployments (by 2026-09-04)
Meera Desai: Provide current data residency requirements and list of restricted regions (by 2026-09-03)
Jonah McKee: Send list of top 5 control mappings they need evidence for (by 2026-09-07)
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 and ISO artifacts + Trust Center invite
Schedule deep-dive with SRE team for KMS integration and on-prem proof-of-concept (week of 2026-09-13)
Customer to provide control priority list and residency constraints
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park, Sofia Martinez, Calvin Lee (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Meera Desai, Jonah McKee, Priya Anand (Bryteway)

Summary: quick readout of Redwood security posture artifacts and initial mapping to Bryteway controls. A few clarifying questions about KMS flows and audit log retention windows.

[00:00] Ethan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Ethan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, i'll hand over to Sofia and Calvin for the technical pieces, but quick goal for today is to go over our SOC 2/ISO artifacts, trust center access, and the high level KMS / RBAC options so you can map controls — anything i missed?

[00:28] Liam O'Connor: no that's good, thanks. we're particularly sensitive to log retention and key management, and we want to confirm residency for a few EU workloads. also curious on what you can share for auditor review.

[01:03] Sofia Martinez: cool, i'll start with the SOC 2 side — we have a SOC 2 Type II report covering the period jan to june 2026, it includes our control matrix and control tests. we can share the redacted report; the Trust Center has the full evidence catalog and several control mappings already pre-populated. note: access is role based so we'll need an account to invite you.

[01:36] Jonah McKee: when you say "evidence catalog" is that live docs or a bundle we can hand to our auditors?

[01:45] Sofia Martinez: it's both — there's downloadable bundles for auditor review and a live portal with audit logs, configuration snapshots. some items are redacted for customer privacy, but standard SOC artifacts are available.

[02:10] Priya Anand: any known gaps against ISO 27001 we should be aware of? we plan to pursue ISO next quarter so we need the mapping now.

[02:22] Calvin Lee: yep, so our platform has an ISO 27001 controls mapping in the trust doc. most customers see a handful of control areas that need customer-side evidence: e.g., asset inventory for customer-managed hosts, and SSO configuration proofs. Redwood provides the server-side operational evidence. we'll share the mapping sheet, which you can import into your compliance tracker.

[02:55] Meera Desai: okay. on the KMS piece — we run all keys in our KMS, and we want to ensure that Redwood never holds plaintext keys. what's supported?

[03:08] Sofia Martinez: we support a bring-your-own-key model. for Private deployments we can integrate with your cloud KMS via customer-managed keys and envelope encryption. for hosted we offer a customer key option via HSM-backed KMS rotation. small caveat: for some older model variants we still need temporary ephemeral keys for caching in the runtime, but we can show the exact flow.

[03:40] Liam O'Connor: ephemeral keys for runtime cache — can you describe that flow? i want to make sure it meets our auditors.

[03:48] Calvin Lee: absolutely. short version: we use envelope encryption — your master key never leaves your KMS. a per-deployment data key is generated and encrypted with your master; the data key is used by the inference runtime but stored encrypted at rest. when running, the runtime asks the KMS to decrypt the data key in memory only. we also rotate data keys on a schedule. sometimes transcripts or mem- hm, KV cache entries, may be buffered in memory but never written key plaintext to persistent storage.

[04:30] Priya Anand: is the KMS flow different for on-prem private installs?

[04:38] Sofia Martinez: on-prem you can provide an HSM or a local KMS endpoint — we support PKCS11 and vendor-specific plugins; the same envelope model applies. for air-gapped installs we do an offline key wrap process during bootstrapping.

[05:05] Jonah McKee: great. audit logs — what retention windows do you support and can we export them into our SIEM?

[05:15] Calvin Lee: yes, logs are exportable via S3 or syslog forwarders, and you can pull them via API. default retention is 90 days in hosted, but we have tiers for 1yr and multi-year on dedicated plans. for Private you control retention entirely. we also provide immutable write-once archives for compliance snapshots.

[05:50] Meera Desai: are PII fields redacted from logs by default? we can't have raw customer content in logs.

[06:00] Sofia Martinez: good question. we do metadata-only logging for user content in production by default — content-level logs are suppressed unless you enable debug. when debug is enabled that's captured under a different retention policy and flagged in the trust center; we can show you how to restrict that.

[06:28] Liam O'Connor: residency — we have EU-only datasets, we need guaranteed region pinning and a paper trail for auditors. how do you enforce region residency?

[06:40] Ethan Park: we support region pinning in Dedicated and Private. hosted also supports region selection but for strict EU-only legal constraints we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can lock capacity to a region and opt out of cross-region fallback. we'll include the routing policy text in the attachment.

[07:05] Priya Anand: what's the fallback policy if capacity is low? i.e. automatic fallback to a different region?

[07:13] Calvin Lee: by default we have smart routing to maintain latency and uptime, but for compliance customers we have a hard pin option — that'll disable cross-region failover. it's part of the Dedicated SLA config.

[07:35] Jonah McKee: ok, can you provide the exact language for the SLA and the tradeoffs? our legal team will want to review the failure scenarios.

[07:44] Ethan Park: yes, we'll add the SLA excerpt to the artifact pack.

[07:50] Meera Desai: about SSO — we use Okta with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning, do you support SCIM for groups and RBAC sync?

[07:59] Sofia Martinez: yes, we support full SAML + SCIM workflows. SCIM provisioning supports group mappings to RBAC roles; we can provide templates and a test tenant. minor caveat: on some older on-prem consoles the SCIM endpoint needs a short manual patch but that's rare.

[08:25] Liam O'Connor: can we get an example mapping? we want auditors to see the roles -> controls relationship.

[08:31] Calvin Lee: yes, there's a Roles->Control table in the Trust Center. sample: "Security Admin" maps to control A.9.2 (sample control), and that role has specific audit log privileges. we'll include a sample mapping csv.

[08:55] Priya Anand: auditors always ask for separation of duties evidence. how do you show that?

[09:02] Sofia Martinez: we have change logs for role grants, MFA enforcement, and admin actions that are timestamped and exportable. those are in the trust center and you can pull them as part of your evidence bundle.

[09:25] Jonah McKee: any red flags we should be aware of before we hand this to external assessors?

[09:32] Calvin Lee: nothing blocking. two items to flag: 1) if you enable debug captures for troubleshooting there's extra logs with more content; you should route that to a secure bucket and provide access controls. 2) if you opt for model variants that are older quantized formats some runtime telemetry is different — we'll show the telemetry mapping.

[10:00] Meera Desai: on the model telemetry, can you guarantee no PII leaves the VPC?

[10:08] Sofia Martinez: for Private deployments yes — all inference traffic remains in your VPC. for Hosted we do not surface PII to third parties, but we recommend tokens or pseudonymization if you have strict requirements.

[10:30] Liam O'Connor: let's talk about the control mapping — can you walk us through an example mapping for encryption controls?

[10:38] Calvin Lee: absolutely. encryption at rest: Redwood provides server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (CMEK) for dedicated/private. control mapping includes KMS key lifecycle (rotation), access guards (RBAC), and audit logs for key usage. we'll provide the mapping rows: control id, evidence type, where to find it in Trust Center.

[11:05] Ethan Park: quick commercial note — Dedicated customers get 1 year trace retention and SLA artifacts baked into the contract; that's sometimes useful for negotiations.

[11:17] Liam O'Connor: noted.

[11:20] Meera Desai: regarding the evidence portal, can we create read-only auditor accounts or time-bound access?

[11:27] Sofia Martinez: yes, we support time-bound auditor accounts and justification fields. auditors can be scoped to a subset of evidence. we also support signed download links with short TTL.

[11:42] Priya Anand: what formats are logs and evidence downloadable as? PDF, CSV, parquet?

[11:49] Calvin Lee: logs: JSON/NDJSON, CSV export for certain tables, and parquet for large exports. evidence bundles are PDF and archived JSON metadata.

[12:10] Jonah McKee: there was mention earlier of redaction — how do you prove redaction to an auditor?

[12:18] Sofia Martinez: redaction is logged: when an artifact is redacted we keep a checksum, an explanation and who approved it. that metadata is included in the evidence bundle so auditors can see what was removed and why.

[12:40] Liam O'Connor: any third-party pen-test results available?

[12:46] Ethan Park: yes, we publish a summary of our latest penetration test and a redacted report in the Trust Center. full reports can be provided under an NDA.

[12:55] Meera Desai: ok, switching back to residency — we need EEA-only processing and also a US-only dataset for different customers. can you do both under one account?

[13:05] Calvin Lee: you can partition workloads by region and set routing policies per API key or project. we recommend separate projects for strict legal separation which also makes auditing simpler.

[13:28] Priya Anand: on tokenization — we want to ensure logs do not contain raw inputs. do you provide built-in redaction for inputs or is it on us?

[13:36] Sofia Martinez: we have input redaction features you can enable per project. by default we mask out long text fields from logs and only keep minimal metadata, but you should test with your sample workflows.

[13:58] Jonah McKee: sample test — will Redwood run a bench with our keys integrated? we want to validate latency impact of KMS calls.

[14:07] Calvin Lee: yes we can run a bench. propose we do a short POC: integrate customer KMS in a private staging deploy and run throughput/latency tests with typical request shapes. that will show the round-trip cost.

[14:30] Liam O'Connor: timeline?

[14:33] Ethan Park: target week of 2026-09-13 for the tech deep-dive + bench, if that works for you.

[14:40] Meera Desai: sounds good. we'll confirm internal availability.

[14:50] Priya Anand: curious about log integrity — do you support signed logs or WORM storage?

[14:57] Calvin Lee: we support immutable WORM archives and signed digests for archived evidence. for active logs we can emit signed integrity checks on rotation.

[15:20] Jonah McKee: competitor question — has anyone tried using other managed inference providers with FIPS HSMs, any major differences?

[15:30] Sofia Martinez: differences tend to be around how much control you get over the runtime and whether they permit custom KMS plugins; Redwood supports both managed and private patterns to cover that gap.

[15:48] Liam O'Connor: ok, anything about data subject requests or deletion proofs? auditors will ask for proof of deletion.

[15:56] Sofia Martinez: yes we have deletion logs and a deletion API with change logs and retention overrides. deletion requests generate an auditable event that's stored in the trust center.

[16:18] Ethan Park: i'm going to run through the agreed artifacts and next steps quickly so we're aligned — 1) we'll share SOC2 type II and Trust Center invite, 2) Sofia will create the KMS integration note, 3) schedule the deep-dive bench, 4) Bryteway to send control priority list.

[16:42] Liam O'Connor: that matches our view. one follow-up — is there a cost implication to extended log retention and auditor snapshots?

[16:51] Ethan Park: yes, long-term retention and additional immutable archives are add-ons on Dedicated and hosted tiers. we'll include pricing ranges in the follow-up email.

[17:05] Meera Desai: any quick notes about encryption algorithms and FIPS compliance? we may need FIPS 140-2 validated modules.

[17:14] Calvin Lee: we can provide FIPS-validated HSM integrations in Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted standard may not be FIPS-validated by default. we'll call that out in the artifact pack.

[17:35] Priya Anand: auditors also ask for key rotation frequency and proof. what's default?

[17:41] Sofia Martinez: default rotation is 90 days for data keys, and 1 year for master keys, configurable to your policy. rotation events are logged with key identifiers.

[18:02] Jonah McKee: ok great. if we get the SOC2 report and examples this week we can start building the mapping doc internally.

[18:10] Ethan Park: we'll send today and include sample mappings and the trust center invite.

[18:20] Liam O'Connor: perfect. anything else from the team?

[18:25] Meera Desai: no, just want the bench scheduled.

[18:28] Calvin Lee: noted, we'll reach out with proposed slots.

[18:33] Ethan Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

[18:38] [end of core conversation — remaining minutes used for calendar syncs and a quick off-record question about billing]
questions: Can Redwood provide SOC2 Type II and redacted ISO evidence?
How does KMS integration work for Private vs Hosted?
What are the log retention tiers and export formats?
Can auditor accounts be time-bound and scoped?
Is region pinning and hard-failover available for EU-only workloads?
